newsitem.title: USA: NYC says state comptroller withdraws four audits.
newsitem.headline: NYC says state comptroller withdraws four audits.

text.p: New York City Deputy Mayor Randy Mastro on Friday said the state comptroller had agreed to withdraw four audits that the Giuliani Administration had blocked, claiming they were politically motivated.

Mastro told reporters at City Hall that in return New York City's Republican Mayor Giuliani had agreed to cooperate with other audits that the city said covered performance issues that were linked to financial concerns, the sphere traditionally examined by the state comptroller. The other audits will not be completed until after the November mayoral elections, Mastro added.
"He has withdrawn certain audits that we found very offensive and polictically motivated," Mastro said, referring to H. Carl McCall, the state comptroller.

The audits that were withdrawn covered the police, sanitation and human resources departments and one on how the city is prepared to deal with computer problems that could arise at the beginning of the year 2000, explained a spokeswoman for the mayor.

McCall, a Democrat, has said he is considering running for governor, and Mastro said some of the audits the state comptroller's staff had begun raised questions about McCall's objectivity as they did not seem to be directed at financial issues.
The state comptroller said the agreement with the Giuliani Administration avoided a potentially costly legal battle, and stressed that his staff's work was objective.

"These audits--just like the hundreds of other audits underway in cities and towns around the state and in state agencies--will be conducted with the highest standard of integrity with the goal of serving the people of New York," McCall said, in prepared remarks. He noted his auditors can resume their work in New York City immediately.

Mastro said it was not realistic to expect the state comptroller to recuse himself from all audits, and noted that in future, he will be told about any new audits at the outset by a staff counsel for the state comptroller. The deputy mayor said the city always had cooperated with fiscal audits and would continue to do so.

Both Mastro and McCall saluted City Council Speaker Peter Vallone for helping to resolve the dispute. Vallone, in prepared remarks, said "This agreement represents a balanced, fair-minded approach to the interests and responsibilities of the mayor and the state comptroller."
